intent.summary: Sustainable timber frame repair using traditional joinery methods to splice defective timber and replace missing rails with matching timber stock.

steps.title: Secure frame and work area
steps.description: Inspect the timber frame corner stability and secure the area with temporary props if necessary.

steps.title: Record member dimensions
steps.description: Measure surviving rail cross-sections, mortise depths, and exact bay spans to draft cutting profiles.

steps.title: Stock selection and sizing
steps.description: Select seasoned timber matching the original species and rip to rough dimensions for infills and splice material.

steps.title: Scarf repair defective rail
steps.description: Cut back defective timber on the left outer rail and fit a traditional scarf joint with matching wood.

steps.title: Fabricate upper inner rail
steps.description: Cut tenons and chamfers on replacement stock for the missing upper inner right rail.

steps.title: Fabricate lower middle rail
steps.description: Cut tenons and matching profiles for the missing lower middle right rail member.

steps.title: Clean frame mortises
steps.description: Clear debris, old rotted tenon fragments, and remnant pegs from open receiving mortises.

steps.title: Fit new timber rails
steps.description: Dry-fit new timber rails into receiving mortises, adjust shoulder seating, and align flush.

steps.title: Peg and lock joints
steps.description: Bore peg holes and drive drawbore hardwood pegs to lock the scarfed repair and replacement tenons.

steps.title: Apply protective timber finish
steps.description: Apply a breathable natural oil finish across new members and exposed cut repairs.

intent.summary: Continuous timber rail replacement restoring structural triangulation across both bays with precision-milled scanned joinery and traditional draw-bored pegging.

steps.title: Remove Upper Rail Middle Right
steps.description: Carefully unpin and demount the damaged Upper Rail Middle Right from its joints at the intermediate post and Diagonal Brace Right, preserving surrounding historic mortises.
toolsRequired: Japanese pull saw (for cutting damaged pegs if jammed)
steps.expectedOutcome: The damaged upper rail middle right is removed cleanly without damage or expansion to the original mortises in the intermediate post and brace.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear heavy leather work gloves and eye protection; support the member during release to prevent sudden drops.

justification.rationale: Demounting the damaged member addresses cond_mt763rxz015 while respecting axis_1 (Material Authenticity) by safeguarding the surrounding historic joinery.

steps.title: Clean and inspect mortises
steps.description: Clean out debris, loose wood fibres, and historic peg remnants from the receiving mortises and housings on the corner post, intermediate post, and brace.
steps.expectedOutcome: All receiving mortises and housings are clean, free of organic detritus and old peg fragments, and ready for accurate templating.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear safety glasses and a dust mask when chiseling and blowing out old wood debris.

justification.rationale: Cleaning the historic sockets reveals the true bearing faces needed to ensure axis_2 (Structural Performance) for the incoming rail.

steps.title: Measure span and joint layout
steps.description: Take direct site dimensions across both bays from the corner post through the intermediate post to determine total length, shoulder positions, and joint profiles.
steps.expectedOutcome: Exact span measurements, shoulder distances, and mortise depth profiles are recorded onto a story stick.

justification.rationale: Direct site templating accounts for racking and out-of-square conditions across the bays, rectifying missing member cond_mt70rqai002 and broken joint cond_mt763rxz015.

steps.title: Cut continuous rail and joints
steps.description: Cut a single continuous timber member to overall length, shaping the end tenons and intermediate housing/lap joint to fit around the intermediate post.
toolsRequired: Traditional timber framing handsaw (Ryoba or hand rip saw)
materialsRequired: 1x seasoned historic-matching oak beam (dimensioned to bay span)
steps.expectedOutcome: A continuous timber rail is cut to length with square shoulders, accurate end tenons, and an intermediate lap/housing matching the intermediate post.
steps.safetyNotes: Keep hands behind the cutting edges of timber slicks and chisels; secure timber firmly on sawhorses.

justification.rationale: Fabricating a continuous structural timber member restores rigidity across both bays (axis_2) while maintaining historic carpentry traditions (axis_4).

steps.title: Dry fit continuous rail
steps.description: Offer up the new timber rail across both bays to verify seating, joint alignment, squareness, and tenon depth before fixing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The continuous rail seats flush against all posts and braces with tight joint shoulders and plumb alignment.
steps.safetyNotes: Heavy lifting required; use two people to lift and maneuver the timber into place to avoid strain.

justification.rationale: Dry fitting verifies tight structural bearing (axis_2) and visual continuity (axis_6) before irreversible pegging.

steps.title: Install and peg rail
steps.description: Seat the continuous rail fully into all housings, drill peg holes offset for draw-boring, and secure with tapered hardwood pegs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The rail is permanently locked into the frame with draw-bored oak pegs pulled tight against all shoulders and trimmed flush.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection when driving cleft pegs and operating the auger.

justification.rationale: Draw-boring with cleft oak pegs mechanically pulls the frame tight, achieving optimal structural integrity (axis_2) using authentic historic methods (axis_1, axis_4).

steps.title: Mill Diagonal Brace Right joint
steps.description: Mill back the damaged contact face and joint seat on Diagonal Brace Right to establish a clean, sound geometric interface for the repair.

steps.title: Scan milled Diagonal Brace Right
steps.description: 3D scan the freshly milled joint area on Diagonal Brace Right to capture precise surface geometry and alignment references for fabrication.

steps.title: Mill new timber joint
steps.description: Mill the new timber rail joint profile to exact geometry derived from the 3D scan data, ensuring seamless mating with Diagonal Brace Right.

steps.title: Sand milled joint surfaces
steps.description: Sand the milled joint faces to remove tool ridges, tear-out, and machining marks, ensuring a clean and precise mating surface before dry assembly.

steps.title: Remove damaged middle rail
steps.description: Carefully unpin and demount the damaged Upper Rail Middle Right from its housings, preserving adjacent historic timber.
toolsRequired: Flat pry bar with timber protective backing
steps.expectedOutcome: The damaged upper middle rail is completely extracted from its housings without inflicting damage on adjacent posts or braces.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and heavy work gloves; be alert to sudden release of loose timber under residual tension.

justification.rationale: Demounting the damaged member addresses joint condition cond_mt763rxz015 while preserving surrounding historic timber fabric in accordance with axis_1.

steps.title: Shore and brace diagonal timber
steps.description: Install temporary props and screw clamps on Diagonal Brace Right to prevent movement and maintain frame plumb during joint remediation.
steps.expectedOutcome: Diagonal Brace Right is securely supported and plumb, prevented from slipping or warping during joint remediation.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure props are seated on stable, load-bearing ground; do not overtighten clamps.

justification.rationale: Ensures structural stability (axis_2) of the unsupported diagonal brace once the constraining rail is removed.

steps.title: Clean and inspect mortises
steps.description: Clear out debris, dirt, and historic peg remnants from the receiving mortises on the corner post, intermediate post, and brace.
toolsRequired: Shop vacuum / handheld stiff bristle brush
steps.expectedOutcome: Mortise pockets and housings are completely clear of rotten wood, loose debris, and sheared peg remnants.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear a dust mask and safety goggles when chiseling and brushing old debris.

justification.rationale: Clearing the mortises allows sound seating of new timber and accurate inspection of historic substrate surfaces.

steps.title: Measure span and joint layout
steps.description: Record exact span dimensions and shoulder positions across both bays from corner post to end post.
steps.expectedOutcome: Accurate shoulder-to-shoulder and overall span dimensions are recorded onto a layout rod across both bays.

justification.rationale: Accurate recording of dimensions across the bays resolves the missing member cond_mt70rqai002 and ensures proper continuous geometry.

steps.title: Mill diagonal brace joint seat
steps.description: Mill back the damaged contact face and joint seat on Diagonal Brace Right in-situ to establish a sound reference surface.
toolsRequired: Plunge router with guide track and flat-bottom bit
steps.expectedOutcome: The damaged joint contact face on the diagonal brace is milled flat, clean, and square to serve as a reliable reference plane.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye and hearing protection, and a dust mask when operating the router in-situ.

justification.rationale: In-situ milling remediates the compromised joint face of cond_mt763rxz015 while minimizing the removal of sound historic timber.

steps.title: Scan milled brace joint
steps.description: 3D scan the freshly milled interface on Diagonal Brace Right to capture exact surface coordinates for CAM toolpath generation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A dense, high-accuracy 3D point cloud and mesh of the milled brace interface is generated.

justification.rationale: Capturing the exact scanned geometry allows custom CAM fabrication for a precise, structurally sound interlocking joint.

steps.title: Dimension rail blank and tenons
steps.description: Dimension a single continuous timber blank spanning both bays, roughing out end tenons and the intermediate post housing.
materialsRequired: Green/seasoned structural oak timber beam (sized to span both bays)
steps.expectedOutcome: Continuous timber blank is squared to dimensions with tenon shoulders and center housing roughed out.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear ear and eye protection; use proper team lifting techniques for heavy structural timber.

justification.rationale: Prepares the single continuous replacement member to resolve missing rail cond_mt70rqai002 and structurally bridge the corner frame.

steps.title: CNC mill mating rail joint
steps.description: CNC mill the mating joint profile on the rail blank using toolpaths calculated directly from the brace 3D scan.
steps.expectedOutcome: The mating joint face on the rail blank is CNC milled to an exact mirror match of the 3D-scanned brace geometry.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure CNC enclosure and emergency stops are operational; wear ear and eye protection.

justification.rationale: Direct CAM translation ensures perfect structural bearing between the new continuous rail and existing diagonal brace.

steps.title: Pare and deburr joint faces
steps.description: Hand-pare joint shoulders with a wide framing chisel and lightly deburr milled surfaces using a flat backing block to keep arrises sharp.
steps.expectedOutcome: Joint shoulders are crisp, clean, and free of toolpath burrs with perfectly square arrises.
steps.safetyNotes: Always chisel away from body and keep hands behind the cutting edge.

justification.rationale: Hand-refining the joint honors traditional timber craftsmanship standards (axis_4) and guarantees gapless joinery.

steps.title: Dry fit continuous rail
steps.description: Offer up the continuous rail across both bays to test seating, alignment, tenon engagement, and shoulder contact.
steps.expectedOutcome: The continuous rail seats cleanly across corner post, intermediate post, and brace, confirming full shoulder contact without binding.
steps.safetyNotes: Two-person lift required to safely handle the long timber rail into position.

justification.rationale: Verifies that the multi-point joinery fits without imposing unwanted stress across the frame before final pinning.

steps.title: Install and peg rail
steps.description: Drive the rail fully into position, drill offset draw-bore peg holes, and lock all connections with tapered cleft oak pegs.
toolsRequired: Heavy timber framing auger / drill (18mm bit)
steps.expectedOutcome: All tenons are draw-bored and permanently secured with cleft oak pegs driven tight and trimmed flush.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection when striking timber pegs and drilling deep holes.

justification.rationale: Draw-bore pegging pulls the joints completely tight, permanently securing the new rail and restoring authentic timber joinery (axis_1, axis_4).

steps.title: Remove damaged middle rail
steps.description: Back out existing wooden pegs and carefully ease the damaged middle rail tenons out of the mortises without fracturing surrounding timber.
toolsRequired: Pry bar with protective timber scrap padding
steps.expectedOutcome: The damaged upper_rail_middle_right is extracted intact from surrounding mortises without damage to the intermediate post or brace joints.
steps.safetyNotes: Eye protection recommended; ensure adequate support for the rail during removal to prevent dropping.

justification.rationale: Directly resolves cond_mt763rxz015 by removing the structurally compromised rail section while safeguarding adjacent authentic historic members per axis_1.

steps.title: Inspect and clean mortises
steps.description: Clean out debris, degraded fibers, and old peg remnants from the housing and mortises in the corner post, intermediate post, and brace intersection.
toolsRequired: Shop vacuum or stiff bristle brush
steps.expectedOutcome: Mortise pockets and housings in the corner post, intermediate post, and brace are clean, square, and free of degraded fibers and peg debris.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and work gloves when clearing out mortises with sharp chisels.

justification.rationale: Ensures clean bearing surfaces and accurate housing geometry required for strong structural performance (axis_2) of the replacement rail.

steps.title: Dimension replacement timber
steps.description: Select and dress a single length of seasoned timber matching the original cross-section to span continuously across both bays.
materialsRequired: Seasoned matching timber beam (species-matched, sized to original cross-section and full two-bay length)
steps.expectedOutcome: A continuous seasoned timber is planed and squared to exact cross-sectional dimensions matching the original frame profiles.
steps.safetyNotes: Dust mask recommended while planing or sawing seasoned hardwoods.

justification.rationale: Prepares the raw replacement stock to match historic dimensions and structural capacity across both bays, addressing missing and damaged sections in one continuous member.

steps.title: Scribe and cut joinery
steps.description: Scribe positions directly against the posts and brace, then cut matching end tenons, intermediate lap/pass-through mortises, and shoulder bevels.
toolsRequired: Ryoba Japanese pull saw or tenon saw
steps.expectedOutcome: All tenons, shoulders, and lap joints are cut accurately to match existing frame housings with crisp, tight tolerances.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure hands remain behind cutting edges; secure the timber stock firmly during joinery cutting.

justification.rationale: Executes traditional joinery interfaces to restore structural connectivity and historical authenticity across the right upper wall frame.

steps.title: Dry fit continuous rail
steps.description: Offer the full-length replacement timber into position to verify joint alignment, squareness, and flush seating against all bearing faces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The continuous rail seats flush against all posts and brace faces with full bearing contact and level alignment.
steps.safetyNotes: Team lift required to safely position and hold the long timber member.

justification.rationale: Validates geometry and fitment before final fastening, preventing structural binding or damaged mortises during final assembly.

steps.title: Fasten and peg joints
steps.description: Seat the continuous timber fully home and drive draw-bored wooden pegs through the joint connections to lock the assembly rigidly.
materialsRequired: Cleft oak or matching hardwood trunnels/pegs (tapered, octagonal/round, 18mm diameter)
steps.expectedOutcome: The continuous rail is securely locked in place with draw-bored trunnels seated flush and tight across all intermediate and corner joints.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear safety glasses when driving pegs with a heavy mallet.

justification.rationale: Completes the structural reinstatement, resolving missing member cond_mt70rqai002 and replacing damaged joint cond_mt763rxz015 using traditional draw-boring techniques.

steps.title: Apply protective finish
steps.description: Apply breathable timber treatment or finish, blending the tone of the new replacement timber with the adjacent weathered historic frame.
materialsRequired: Breathable exterior timber oil or linseed/wax finish (blended tone, 500ml)
steps.expectedOutcome: The replacement timber is fully treated with a breathable finish that blends visually with the historic weathered frame.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure adequate ventilation; dispose of oil-soaked rags in a sealed, water-filled metal container to prevent spontaneous combustion.

justification.rationale: Protects new timber from ecological weathering while harmonizing the visual contrast between new and historic frame members per axis_6.

intent.summary: Hybrid human-robot repair workflow: robotic precision marking and scanning combined with skilled manual cutting and timber joint assembly.

steps.title: [Human] Joint prep and datums
steps.description: Manually clean decayed fibers and debris from joint housings with chisels and brass brushes. Affix high-contrast optical target markers to the timber frame to establish reference datums for robot coordinate alignment.

steps.title: [Robot] 3D optical scanning
steps.description: Run an automated robotic scanning trajectory using a structured-light 3D scanner to capture sub-millimeter geometry and deformation of the receiving mortises and frame interfaces.

steps.title: [Human] CAM and toolpath simulation
steps.description: Process point cloud data to generate parametric joint geometry, align wood grain orientation with the parent frame, and simulate collision-free milling toolpaths.

steps.title: [Robot] 5-axis timber milling
steps.description: Execute robotic 5-axis spindle milling on a secured seasoned timber blank, roughing and finishing the custom tenons, housings, and continuous profile to matched tolerances.

steps.title: [Human] Dry fit and paring
steps.description: Remove robotic machining scallops with fine hand chisels, check fit against the physical frame, and manually pare mating faces for tight grain-to-grain contact.

steps.title: [Human] Adhesive assembly and clamping
steps.description: Apply structural 2-part polyurethane or timber adhesive to the joint pockets, insert the continuous timber piece into intermediate post and diagonal brace mortises, and torque bar clamps to draw the joint shut.

steps.title: [Human] Draw-bore pegging and oiling
steps.description: Drill offset draw-bore peg holes through the tenon joints, drive riven oak trunnels with a mallet, cut pegs flush, and apply a breathable linseed oil protective finish.

steps.title: Assess timber damage
steps.description: Inspect damaged and missing timber members with visual assessment, sounding hammer, and awl probes to determine sound wood boundaries and extent of decay.

steps.title: Formulate repair plan
steps.description: Establish repair parameters, reference datums, and working sequencing for the replacement splice and missing member reconstruction.

steps.title: Design repair joint
steps.description: Model parametric joint geometries (scarf / notched thrust joint) tailored to the frame geometry and remaining sound timber cross-section.

steps.title: [Robot] Mill guide markings
steps.description: Use a robotic milling spindle or laser stylus to etch high-precision reference cut lines and depth stops directly onto the damaged historic member.

steps.title: [Human] Cut repair joint
steps.description: Manually cut away decayed timber along the robot-milled reference kerfs using Japanese pull saws and hand paring chisels.

steps.title: [Robot] Scan cut surface
steps.description: Perform high-resolution 3D optical surface scanning of the newly prepared cut surface to capture as-built manual cut variations and deviations.

steps.title: Compute adaptive joint toolpath
steps.description: Generate adaptive CAD/CAM geometry and toolpaths for the mating timber piece based directly on the 3D scan point cloud of the cut interface.

steps.title: Fabricate new timber piece
steps.description: Machine the matching new timber replacement piece with robotic 5-axis milling and fine hand paring to match the scanned mating surface.

steps.title: [Human] Assemble into structure
steps.description: Dry-fit, apply structural timber adhesive, clamp assembly into the structure, and lock the joint with riven oak draw-bore pegs.

strategies.label: Full Rail Replacement - Lower Outer Left

steps.title: Record and measure joint geometry
steps.description: Measure cross-section dimensions, overall length, tenon lengths, and peg hole locations from the existing defective rail and adjacent post mortises.

steps.title: Demount defective rail
steps.description: Drill or punch out retaining pegs and ease the defective rail out of the mortises in the end post and intermediate post.

steps.title: Clean and dress post mortises
steps.description: Scrape and pare old debris or decayed wood fibres from inside the receiving mortises in both posts.

steps.title: Mill replacement timber stock
steps.description: Rip and plane new sound timber stock to match the cross-sectional dimensions of the historic rail.

steps.title: Cut tenons and shoulders
steps.description: Layout and cut tenons on both ends of the replacement rail with Japanese pull saw and framing chisels.

steps.title: Dry-fit replacement rail
steps.description: Insert the new rail into the left end post and intermediate post to verify shoulder alignment, plumb, and fit.

steps.title: Install and secure with pegs
steps.description: Seat the rail home into both mortises, drill peg holes with drawbore offset, and drive riven wooden pegs to lock the assembly.

steps.title: Dry-fit truss assembly
steps.description: Temporarily hoist and dry-fit the timber diagonal between Top Beam Side and Corner Post Front Left using timber props, wedged temporary stays, and hemp rope lashings to verify pitch angles, bearing alignment, and clearance.
steps.expectedOutcome: All truss components and steel brackets temporarily held in position, verifying flush alignment and clearance before final assembly.
steps.safetyNotes: Support suspended timber members securely to avoid pinch hazards or dropping overhead items.

justification.rationale: Dry-fitting confirms geometry and load paths prior to torquing, preventing unexpected misalignment or strain on the historic frame.

steps.title: Fit timber clamping yokes
steps.description: Assemble two-piece split timber yoke collars (bridles) around Top Beam Side and Corner Post Front Left over protective pads. Secure the collar halves around the exterior using drawbore hardwood pegs and cross-wedged timber tension keys, completely free of metal bolts or fittings.
materialsRequired: Fabricated steel friction collars and plate yokes
Grade 8.8 zinc-plated threaded rods with matching nuts and washers
steps.expectedOutcome: External steel collar assemblies loosely secured around top_beam_side and posts with protective pads correctly sandwiched between steel and timber.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear protective gloves to handle steel plates and prevent thread-snagging injuries.

justification.rationale: Non-destructive friction collars provide lateral and vertical bracing load capacity while maintaining complete reversibility without drilling into historic timber.

steps.title: Seat diagonal in collar nodes
steps.description: Seat the timber diagonal strut ends firmly into the abutment seats of the upper collar on Top Beam Side and the lower collar on Corner Post Front Left. Check full face contact with feeler gauges.
materialsRequired: M12 grade 8.8 retention bolts with nylon-insert locknuts
steps.expectedOutcome: New timber diagonals and chords are seated fully within the bracket shoes of the friction collars.
steps.safetyNotes: Maintain firm two-person handling when lifting and positioning heavy timber members overhead.

justification.rationale: Completes the load-bearing truss geometry that counteracts lateral racking tendencies along the side frame.

steps.title: Drive wedges to preload truss
steps.description: Drive the hardwood folding wedges into the collar node pockets to pretension the diagonal strut in compression between the Top Beam Side and Corner Post Front Left.
steps.expectedOutcome: All collar bolts tightened uniformly to specified torque values, establishing full frictional shear engagement without compressing wood fibers.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure stable platform stance while applying torque overhead.

justification.rationale: Even, controlled torque prevents localized crushing of historic fibers while ensuring sufficient frictional resistance for structural stability.

steps.title: Check alignment & wedge tension
steps.description: Check plumb of Corner Post Front Left, level and camber of Top Beam Side, and verify tight bearing of the wedged timber yokes and diagonal strut without any timber indentation or loosening under load.
steps.expectedOutcome: Side frame posts verified plumb, top beam level, and collar friction joints confirmed slip-free under test conditions.
steps.safetyNotes: Clear workspace below before applying test lateral displacement checks.

justification.rationale: Directly verifies mitigation of cond_mt77c59x060 (lateral racking risk) by proving frame rigidity and correct structural geometry.

intent.summary: Emphasize degraded and rotten timber elements by altering sound historic members and introducing new diagonal reinforcements to bypass/relieve decayed sections while displaying decay as historical trace.

Contrast framing strategy: preserve sound historic timber framing and leave weathered elements legible, while introducing crisp, pale contemporary timber infills to clearly distinguish modern intervention from historic fabric.

steps.title: Survey and document geometry
steps.description: Document baseline framing dimensions, joint tolerances, and establish reference datum points across all sound members while recording the undisturbed defective rail.
steps.expectedOutcome: All key frame baseline dimensions, joint tolerances, and reference datum points are recorded without modifying any historic timber.

justification.rationale: Accurate recording of existing frame dimensions ensures subsequent contrast interventions fit precisely while respecting historic geometry (axis_1, axis_4).

steps.title: Surface dress sound frame
steps.description: Clean and crisp-plane all sound posts and beams to uniform, dressed faces, deliberately leaving the degraded lower rail untouched in its weathered state.
steps.expectedOutcome: Sound framing members display crisp, clean dressed surfaces while the weathered lower rail remains intact in its degraded state.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and work gloves when hand-planing and scraping aged timber surfaces.

justification.rationale: Dressing sound frame elements establishes a clear aesthetic baseline that contrasts deliberately with historic patina (axis_6).

steps.title: Measure missing rail pockets
steps.description: Take exact measurements and pocket templates for the missing outer and inner rail slots in the front-left bay.
steps.expectedOutcome: Exact dimensional templates for the missing upper outer and lower inner mortise pockets are verified and documented.

justification.rationale: Precise pocket measurement directly prepares for resolving missing rail conditions cond_mt77c59x05y and cond_mt77c59x05z with snug structural joints (axis_2).

steps.title: Fabricate upper infill rail
steps.description: Dimension and machine a replacement upper rail from pale contemporary timber (such as clear ash or birch), cutting clean tenons to fit the front-left mortise pockets.
steps.expectedOutcome: A newly dimensioned upper infill rail with crisp tenons is fully fabricated ready for trial fitting.
steps.safetyNotes: Keep hands behind sharp cutting edges when chiseling tenon shoulders; wear eye protection.

justification.rationale: Fabricates the replacement rail for cond_mt77c59x05y using modern stock to manifest the deliberate aesthetic contrast (axis_6) while restoring framing unity (axis_2).

steps.title: Fabricate lower infill rail
steps.description: Dimension and machine the matching lower infill rail from pale contemporary timber stock to fit the lower mortise tolerances.
steps.expectedOutcome: A matching contemporary lower infill rail is machined to exact pocket specifications.
steps.safetyNotes: Maintain proper stance and secure the timber blank firmly in a vise during sawing and chiseling.

justification.rationale: Addresses missing rail condition cond_mt77c59x05z by providing a dimensionally exact, clearly distinguishable contemporary member.

steps.title: Finish new infill rails
steps.description: Apply a non-yellowing, matte clear protective seal to the pale infill rails to lock in the light tone and keep the visual break against the aged frame crisp.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both new infill rails have a smooth, sealed modern matte finish highlighting their differentiation from the historic timber.
steps.safetyNotes: Apply sealant in a well-ventilated area and wear protective nitrile gloves.

justification.rationale: Seals the new additions to protect them and visually accentuate the intervention without mimicking historic patina (axis_6, axis_1).

steps.title: Install infill rails
steps.description: Install and fix the contrasting infill rails into the front-left post mortises.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both new infill rails are securely seated and bonded into the front-left post mortises, flush and square.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure fingers are clear of pinch points when tapping rails into post mortises.

justification.rationale: Completes the physical remediation of missing components cond_mt77c59x05y and cond_mt77c59x05z, restoring structural continuity (axis_2).

steps.title: Stiffen side diagonal brace
steps.description: Check and wedge the side diagonal brace tenons to lock the frame against lateral racking without altering its visual patina.
steps.expectedOutcome: Side diagonal brace tenons are driven tight with trimmed wedges, eliminating frame play without altering visible surface patina.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear safety glasses when driving wedges and flush-trimming protruding shim ends.

justification.rationale: Directly resolves lateral racking risk cond_mt77c59x060 by mechanically tightening joint interfaces while preserving historic surfaces (axis_2, axis_1).

steps.title: Final contrast inspection
steps.description: Review framing alignment and visual contrast across the dressed timber, new infills, and undisturbed weathered rail.
steps.expectedOutcome: Overall frame plumbness and the visual harmony between dressed sound members, modern infills, and weathered rail cond_mt77c59x05x are validated.

justification.rationale: Evaluates the completed repair to verify that the intentional contrast strategy (axis_6) and structural rigidity (axis_2) successfully coexist with the preserved defective rail cond_mt77c59x05x.

intent.summary: Infill the central frame opening with timber bracing using traditional notched oblique thrust joints (Brustversatz) to improve lateral stiffness.

steps.title: Layout notch geometry on posts
steps.description: Layout the diagonal line from lower corner_post_front_right to upper middle_post_front. Mark the Brustversatz notch geometry exclusively on the inner faces of the two vertical posts (clearing the horizontal rails completely). Depth marked at 1/3 post depth (approx. 25–30 mm) with a 2° to 3° wedge taper along the entry axis.
steps.expectedOutcome: Thrust angles and notch boundary lines are accurately scribed onto the frame timbers at the specified 1:2 to 1:3 ratio.
steps.safetyNotes: Take care when handling sharp marking knives.

justification.rationale: Accurate layout is critical for achieving optimal bearing contact and structural load transfer according to traditional framing geometry (axis_1, axis_2).

steps.title: Cut thrust mortises into posts
steps.description: Saw the perpendicular thrust shoulders strictly into the inner faces of corner_post_front_right (bottom) and middle_post_front (top) to 1/3 timber depth. Chisel the mortise beds with a 2° to 3° ramp without notching the upper or lower rails.
steps.expectedOutcome: Clean, square Brustversatz thrust notches are carved into the frame timbers with perfectly flat bearing faces.
steps.safetyNotes: Always cut away from body and hands when using framing chisels; wear eye protection.

justification.rationale: Cutting authentic thrust abutment notches directly into the frame resolves cond_mt77c59x060 (lateral racking risk) by creating rigid mechanical load transfer interfaces.

steps.title: Dimension pine strut stock
steps.description: Cross-cut fresh structural pine timber stock matching the frame depth to gross diagonal length, including a 50–75 mm working allowance at each end for laying out the angled Brustversatz thrust shoulders.
steps.expectedOutcome: Timber stock is crosscut to rough overall length with sufficient surplus for end joinery profiling.
steps.safetyNotes: Secure timber stock on sawbenches before cutting.

justification.rationale: Rough dimensioning establishes the raw diagonal member from matching material stock, respecting material authenticity.

steps.title: Cut matching tapered strut ends
steps.description: Cut the matching angled thrust shoulders and tapered heel faces on both ends of the pine strut stock to match the 2°–3° mortise slope, ensuring full-surface bearing once driven fully home.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both ends of the diagonal strut feature precisely cut oblique thrust shoulders and locating tenons matching the receiver notches.
steps.safetyNotes: Clamp timber securely while paring shoulders with chisels and planes.

justification.rationale: Accurate joinery profiling on the strut ensures maximum surface contact area for diagonal thrust compression under wind and racking loads.

steps.title: Dry fit diagonal strut
steps.description: Offer the strut into the opening to check bearing face contact across the full width of both notches.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diagonal strut seats cleanly into both frame notches with full-face bearing contact and no significant gaps.
steps.safetyNotes: Watch for pinch points between strut shoulders and frame abutments during insertion.

justification.rationale: A dry fit verifies that load-bearing faces mate uniformly before permanent boring and fastening take place.

steps.title: Bore drawbore peg holes
steps.description: Bore offset drawbore peg holes through the frame cheeks and strut tenons to draw the joint tight under compression.
steps.expectedOutcome: Offset drawbore holes (1/16 to 1/8 inch offset) are bored through frame mortise walls and strut tenons.
steps.safetyNotes: Keep brace/drill perpendicular and braced to prevent wrist strain or blow-out on timber exit.

justification.rationale: Drawboring mechanically pulls the Brustversatz joint tightly into compression without relying on metallic fasteners, upholding cultural continuity and joint tightness.

steps.title: Drive strut into post mortises
steps.description: Guide the strut between the two posts, drive it home along the slanted bed into the post mortises until full wedge tension is engaged at the thrust faces, then lock with tapered hardwood pegs through the post drawbore holes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The diagonal strut is securely pinned into the frame with driven hardwood pegs, providing full racking restraint.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure clamping devices are firmly seated along the thrust line to avoid sudden slippage.

justification.rationale: Final pegging locks the Brustversatz assembly into place, directly mitigating cond_mt77c59x060 by stiffening the frame against lateral racking.

intent.summary: Preserve maximum historic fabric by executing a Dutchman scarf joint repair on the lower rail, splicing in sound timber and reinstating the tenon connection to the post.
Visible and expressive contemporary intervention celebrating the repair rather than concealing it.

steps.title: Support and prop framing
steps.description: Erect screw jacks or timber props beneath the adjacent framing to safely unload the back-left rail assembly during cutting.
steps.expectedOutcome: The back-left lower rail is fully unloaded and adjacent framing is stably supported without structural deflection.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure props are seated on stable, level footing and secured against accidental slippage.

justification.rationale: Temporary shoring isolates the compromised rail (cond_mt8ds0wk001), safeguarding structural stability (axis_2) while cutting and shaping take place.

steps.title: Cut back decayed rail
steps.description: Establish a clean, square reference line 50mm past all fungal decay. Cut away the rotted timber end using a Wisent 250mm Ryoba saw on the crosscut tooth side.
steps.expectedOutcome: The decayed end of lower_rail_back_left is cleanly severed, exposing completely sound and solid historic timber grain.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and cut-resistant gloves; support cut-off pieces to prevent tearout or dropping.

justification.rationale: Eliminating rotten fiber (cond_mt8ds0wk001) arrests decay while preserving maximum authentic timber stock (axis_1, axis_2).

steps.title: Clean and inspect mortise
steps.description: Scrape and pare old degraded wood and debris from the receiving mortise in the corner post. Check for solid internal bearing faces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The mortise in corner_post_back_left is free of loose rot, dust, and frass, with solid bearing surfaces confirmed.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and a dust mask when clearing dry debris and fungal remnants.

justification.rationale: Ensures the receiving mortise has retained sufficient structural integrity (axis_2) to anchor the replacement tenon securely.

steps.title: Cut scarf on existing rail
steps.description: Lay out and cut an expressive splayed or half-lap scarf joint profile with a 1:4 slope on the sound rail end. Pare the cheek and shoulder dead flat.
steps.expectedOutcome: A precise half-lap scarf joint profile is cut into the sound end of lower_rail_back_left with flat, square bearing faces.
steps.safetyNotes: Always chisel away from the body and hands; ensure sharp edges are handled carefully.

justification.rationale: A traditional scarf joint respects historic timber framing traditions (axis_4) while maximizing surface area for structural repair (axis_1).

steps.title: Fabricate Dutchman splice
steps.description: Dimension a replacement Dutchman block from contrasting dry timber. Cut the complementary scarf slope and form a tenon to fit the post mortise.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new timber Dutchman is shaped with a matching scarf profile on one end and a precisely dimensioned tenon on the other.
steps.safetyNotes: Secure the workpiece firmly in a vise or clamp before sawing and chiseling.

justification.rationale: Fabricating a closely matching replacement component preserves original material continuity (axis_1) and aesthetic harmony (axis_6).

steps.title: Dry fit scarf and tenon
steps.description: Offer up the Dutchman piece into the mortise and scarf joint. Check for tight shoulder contact and seamless face alignment, paring high spots.
steps.expectedOutcome: The scarf and tenon assemble smoothly without binding, showing full, continuous surface contact across all mating joints.
steps.safetyNotes: Use care when paring; avoid forcing timber pieces together which could split historic fibers.

justification.rationale: Precise mechanical bearing is critical to load transfer (axis_2) and reflects master carpentry craftsmanship (axis_4).

steps.title: Glue and clamp splice
steps.description: Apply structural adhesive along the scarf mating cheeks and tenon cheeks. Seat the joint and clamp firmly using F-clamps with protective cauls. Allow full cure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Dutchman splice is clamped firmly into the existing rail with uniform adhesive squeeze-out along the seam.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses when handling structural adhesives. Work in a ventilated area.

justification.rationale: Adhesive bonding provides supplementary shear and tension resistance, restoring full structural capacity (axis_2).

steps.title: Pin joint with staggered pegs
steps.description: Bore 8mm to 10mm drawbore peg holes directly through the overlapping scarf splice and post mortise in a staggered, alternating pattern (horizontal, vertical, horizontal) to ensure pins do not collide internally. Drive faceted dark hardwood pegs (bog oak or walnut), leaving the chamfered heads standing 3mm proud.
toolsRequired: Drill with Makita 8mm/10mm brad point bit
steps.expectedOutcome: Hardwood pegs are driven tightly through offset holes, locking the scarf joint and mortise-tenon connection under tension.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection while drilling and driving pegs.

justification.rationale: Drawbored hardwood pegging represents authentic timber framing methodology (axis_4), ensuring enduring mechanical interlock (axis_1).

steps.title: Flush plane and finish
steps.description: Lightly plane the joint transitions flush while leaving the proud faceted pegs intact. Apply clear matte breathable oil to celebrate the contrasting wood grain and joinery.
steps.expectedOutcome: The repair is perfectly flush with existing rail profiles and treated with an even, breathable protective coating.
steps.safetyNotes: Properly dispose of oil-soaked rags in water or airtight metal containers to prevent spontaneous combustion.

justification.rationale: Provides aesthetic integration (axis_6) and vapor-permeable ecological protection (axis_5) against future moisture-induced decay.

steps.title: Mark spline mortise boundary
steps.description: Trace the run of the split wood on the rail face and lay out parallel baseline mortise marks using a folding ruler and marking gauge.

steps.title: Chisel spline slot
steps.description: Chisel out a clean, flat-bottomed rectangular slot along the split line using narrow bench chisels (8 mm / 14 mm) and a wooden mallet.

steps.title: Cut matching timber spline
steps.description: Rip and crosscut a timber insert from seasoned stock matching species and grain direction to the mortise dimensions using a mini-ryoba pull saw.

steps.title: Dry-fit spline insert
steps.description: Insert the cut spline into the slot without adhesive to test joint tightness, seating depth, and grain orientation.

steps.title: Glue and clamp spline
steps.description: Apply wood adhesive along the split and slot walls, seat the spline, and secure across the rail with two F-clamps for full cure (approx. 30–45 min).

steps.title: Trim spline flush
steps.description: Pare proud spline stock flush with the surrounding rail surface using a wide bevel-edge chisel (26 mm or 38 mm) and finish flat.

steps.title: Clean and prep void
steps.description: Clean out loose timber fibres and dust from the chip on the left end post using a brass wire brush and a small paring chisel to create a solid backing for adhesion.

steps.title: Apply timber infill paste
steps.description: Mix fine wood flour matching the timber species with a reversible binder (or linseed oil putty) to match the surrounding grain tone. Press firmly into the void slightly proud of the surface, ensuring no trapped air pockets. Allow full cure.

steps.title: Scrape and blend flush
steps.description: Once cured, pare down excess infill with a cabinet scraper and blend the boundary with 220-grit abrasive, working strictly in the direction of the grain to avoid scuffing adjacent historic timber.

steps.title: Install temporary shoring
steps.description: Install temporary props and screw jacks adjacent to the corner post to relieve dead loads from the top beams.
steps.expectedOutcome: The overhead top beams are fully supported by temporary props with zero live load resting on the front-left corner post.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure spreading pads rest on solid foundation; verify vertical alignment of jacks to prevent kick-out under load.

justification.rationale: Essential prerequisite to ensure structural stability (axis_2) and prevent catastrophic frame movement while cutting the load-bearing corner post.

steps.title: Assess decay boundary
steps.description: Sound the timber with an awl and measure the full height of decay to determine the cut line in sound wood.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clear, marked boundary line indicating solid, uncompromised wood at least 50mm above all fungal soft rot.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and work gloves when probing decayed wood.

justification.rationale: Locates the exact extent of cond_mt757m7c001 to maximize retention of historic fabric (axis_1) while securing a sound base for structural loading (axis_2).

steps.title: Cut away rotted base
steps.description: Saw through the rotted base of the corner post above the decay zone using a Japanese pull saw.
steps.expectedOutcome: The decayed bottom portion of the corner post is cleanly severed and removed, leaving a square cut across sound timber.
steps.safetyNotes: Support cut offcut to avoid foot injury; wear safety glasses and dust mask.

justification.rationale: Removes the actively degraded wood identified in cond_mt757m7c001 to stop fungal spread and prepare the post for splicing.

steps.title: Clean sill mortise
steps.description: Clean out debris and decayed wood fibers from the sill beam mortise pocket and treat against fungal spores.
steps.expectedOutcome: The sill mortise pocket is free of loose rot and wood debris, and coated with penetrative fungicide.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection, and a P2 respirator during biocide application.

justification.rationale: Sterilizes the contact zone in the sill beam to prevent recurrence of rot and ensure clean bearing for the new timber shoe.

steps.title: Cut post scarf joint
steps.description: Cut and pare a traditional stop-splayed or bladed scarf joint into the sound bottom end of the remaining post.
steps.expectedOutcome: A precisely cut and flat stop-splayed scarf half-lap profile on the bottom of the remaining sound corner post.
steps.safetyNotes: Always chisel away from body and hands; ensure sharp edges are handled with care.

justification.rationale: Executing a traditional carpentry joint maintains cultural continuity (axis_4) and historic authenticity (axis_1) while restoring compressive capacity.

steps.title: Fabricate replacement timber shoe
steps.description: Hew and dimension a replacement timber shoe matching the original post profile, scarf joint, and bottom tenon.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fully shaped replacement timber shoe matching the original post cross-section, scarf profile, and bottom tenon.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and dust mask during sawing and timber shaping.

justification.rationale: Recreates the missing post segment to resolve cond_mt757m7c001, matching the original section profile and joinery standards.

steps.title: Trial fit new shoe
steps.description: Test the fit of the replacement timber shoe into the sill mortise and against the upper post scarf joint.
steps.expectedOutcome: The replacement shoe seats tightly with full surface contact across the scarf face and within the bottom mortise without binding.
steps.safetyNotes: Watch for pinch points between timber members during insertion.

justification.rationale: Verifies load transfer surfaces are true before permanent pegging to prevent point-loading and joint distortion.

steps.title: Fasten scarf joint
steps.description: Lock the scarf joint using draw-bored oak dowels or stainless fasteners to secure the joint under compression.
steps.expectedOutcome: The scarf joint is pulled tight and locked rigidly under tension via draw-bored oak pegs trimmed flush.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection when drilling and driving wooden trunnels.

justification.rationale: Draw-boring provides permanent mechanical interlocking aligned with traditional craft practice (axis_4) and structural requirements (axis_2).

steps.title: Apply preservative finish
steps.description: Apply breathable linseed oil or timber preservative to all newly cut end grain and joint interfaces.
materialsRequired: Boiled linseed oil / breathable timber preservative (250ml)
steps.expectedOutcome: All freshly exposed end-grain and joint faces are saturated with a breathable protective oil finish.
steps.safetyNotes: Properly dispose of oil-soaked rags in water-filled metal containers to avoid spontaneous combustion.

justification.rationale: Protects raw cut surfaces against future moisture ingress and decay while maintaining ecological breathability (axis_5).

steps.title: Strike temporary shoring
steps.description: Gradually de-tension and remove the temporary shoring once the scarf joint is fully secured and bearing load.
steps.expectedOutcome: Temporary props are removed, and dead loads are safely and evenly transferred back onto the repaired corner post.
steps.safetyNotes: De-tension slowly while observing joint deflection and overhead connections for unexpected movement.

justification.rationale: Concludes the repair cycle by returning the frame to full self-supporting structural equilibrium (axis_2).

steps.description: Cross-cut fresh structural pine timber stock matching the frame depth to gross diagonal length, including a 50–75 mm working allowance at each end for laying out the angled Brustversatz thrust shoulders.

justification.rationale: Rough dimensioning establishes the raw diagonal member from matching material stock, respecting material authenticity.

steps.title: Cut matching tapered strut ends
steps.description: Cut the matching angled thrust shoulders and tapered heel faces on both ends of the pine strut stock to match the 2°–3° mortise slope, ensuring full-surface bearing once driven fully home.

steps.title: Dry fit diagonal strut
steps.description: Offer the strut into the opening to check bearing face contact across the full width of both notches.

steps.title: Bore drawbore peg holes

steps.title: Drive strut and lock with pegs
steps.description: Guide the strut into the widened mortise entry by hand, drive it home along the slanted bed with a wooden mallet and protective dead-blow block until full wedge tension is engaged at the thrust faces, then drive tapered hardwood pegs through the drawbore holes.

intent.summary: Conservative structural repair of the timber frame corner: stabilize cracked members, splice sound timber into localized rot at joints, and replace fully degraded rails matching original historic joinery.

steps.title: Shore up corner assembly
steps.description: Install temporary acrow props and load-spreading timber sole plates to relieve structural loads from the corner assembly before opening joints.
steps.expectedOutcome: Temporary structural shoring is securely seated and bearing load off the corner post and connecting plates with zero movement.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear hard hat, steel-toe boots, and gloves; ensure sole plates rest on solid, stable ground before loading props.

justification.rationale: Shoring is essential to maintain structural performance and worker safety by unloading the compromised corner assembly prior to joint intervention.

steps.title: Remove rotten outer left rail
steps.description: Carefully extract the fully decayed outer left lower rail and clean out the receiving mortises without enlarging historic timber walls.
steps.expectedOutcome: The decayed rail is removed and adjacent mortises are cleaned out to sound timber without damage to the surrounding post walls.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear protective gloves and eye protection; be mindful of flying wood fragments and pinch points during levering.

justification.rationale: Addresses cond_mt78kam212eb9aeb by removing unsalvageable decaying timber to stop fungal propagation while preserving the historic mortises.

steps.title: Excavate corner post rot
steps.description: Pare back the surface rot on the corner post using hand chisels and wire brushes until sound, solid heartwood is reached.
steps.expectedOutcome: All soft, decayed sapwood on the corner post is removed, leaving a firm and dry heartwood surface.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear an FFP3/N95 dust mask to avoid inhaling fungal spores and wood dust, along with safety glasses.

justification.rationale: Directly tackles cond_mt8cv1guce64b84e by halting active decay while preserving maximum original fabric on the critical corner post.

steps.title: Preserve corner post wood
steps.description: Apply a breathable borate-based wood preservative and timber consolidant to the exposed sound timber face on the corner post.
steps.expectedOutcome: The excavated corner post timber is thoroughly saturated with preservative and stabilized with consolidant.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure good natural ventilation; wear nitrile chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, and a vapour respirator.

justification.rationale: Provides long-term biological protection and consolidation to the remaining historic core of the corner post following excavation.

steps.title: Stabilize cracks on outer right
steps.description: Clean debris from the cracks on the lower rail outer right, inject timber adhesive, and clamp across the grain until fully cured.
steps.expectedOutcome: Cracks are fully filled with adhesive and pulled closed under clamped pressure with smooth surface squeeze-out cleaned.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear safety glasses during compressed air blowout and protective gloves when handling structural adhesives.

justification.rationale: Resolves cond_mt8nemnq30636f4a conservatively by reinforcing structural integrity without unnecessarily removing sound historic wood.

steps.title: Cut scarf joint on inner right
steps.description: Cut back the rotten tenon end on the inner right rail at a clean angle to prepare for a bladed scarf joint splice.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clean, flat, angled scarf joint surface is cut across the sound section of the inner right rail ready to receive the splice.
steps.safetyNotes: Keep non-dominant hand behind the cutting edge of all hand chisels; wear cut-resistant gloves.

justification.rationale: Addresses cond_mt8d0e18b6f17339 by preparing the rail for a traditional bladed scarf joint, preserving the majority of the original member.

steps.title: Splice inner right tenon
steps.description: Fabricate a matching seasoned timber splice with replacement tenon and secure to the inner right rail using drawbored timber pegs.
steps.expectedOutcome: A mating scarf timber splice with replacement tenon is bonded, drawbored, and firmly pegged into the inner right rail.
steps.safetyNotes: Wear eye protection and secure workpiece in bench vise or clamp while cutting and paring joinery.

justification.rationale: Restores structural load-bearing capacity and authentic joinery to the rail while adhering to traditional carpentry techniques.

steps.title: Fabricate outer left rail
steps.description: Heft and cut a new replacement rail from seasoned oak matching original dimensions and end tenons of the outer left rail.
steps.expectedOutcome: A fully shaped replacement outer left rail with cut end tenons exactly matching original dimensions is completed.
steps.safetyNotes: Ensure timber is securely clamped during saw cuts; wear eye protection and dust mask during planing and shaping.

justification.rationale: Replaces the degraded member (cond_mt78kam212eb9aeb) with an historically accurate, seasoned timber component matching original profiles.

steps.title: Fit and peg rails
steps.description: Offer up both the replacement outer left rail and spliced inner right rail into their mortises, aligning joints and driving tapered wooden pegs.
steps.expectedOutcome: Both rails are seated tight in their mortises with drawbore pegs fully driven and trimmed flush.
steps.safetyNotes: Mind pinch points between heavy timber tenons and mortise shoulders during fitting.

justification.rationale: Re-establishes the complete structural frame corner assembly by locking the repaired and replaced members using traditional drawbore pinning.

steps.title: Strike shoring and inspect
steps.description: Ease and strike temporary shoring, verifying even bearing and joint tight closure across all four repaired members under load.
steps.expectedOutcome: Shoring is removed, with all timber joints fully closed, plumb, and bearing structural load without deflection or cracking.
steps.safetyNotes: De-tension props slowly in small alternating increments to avoid sudden load transfer onto the corner assembly.

justification.rationale: Validates that all addressed conditions have been successfully mitigated and that the entire corner assembly safely carries working dead and live loads.
